## MiFID II Article 16(6) — Record-keeping by investment firms

Article 16(6) requires records sufficient for supervision but states no retention period. The periods come from Article 16(7) for recorded communications and MiFIR Article 25(1) for order and transaction data. Commission Delegated Regulation 2017/565 Article 72 sets the storage-medium conditions.

- **Citation:** [Directive 2014/65/EU, Article 16(6)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2014/65/oj) (European Parliament, Council and Commission)
- **Status:** in force as of 2026-09-18
- **Status note:** Status taken from the Official Journal text; the consolidated version was not compared, because EUR-Lex refuses automated retrieval.
- **Applies to:** Investment firms authorised under MiFID II
- **Cloud relevance:** high
- **Confidence:** medium. Verified 2026-09-18 by claude-opus-5 agent session (not reviewed by counsel). Read the Official Journal texts of Directive 2014/65/EU, Regulation 600/2014 and Delegated Regulation 2017/565 from publications.europa.eu. Consolidated versions not compared, hence medium confidence.
- **Review due:** 2027-03-18

<a id="eu-mifid2-art16-6-dr72"></a>

### Storage medium must reveal every correction and prevent manipulation

`eu-mifid2-art16-6.dr72` · form · applies to Investment firms

Keep records on a medium that the authority can readily access to reconstitute each key stage of a transaction, where corrections and the prior contents are easily ascertainable, and which cannot otherwise be manipulated or altered.

- **Source:** [Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/565, Article 72(1)(a)-(c)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2017/565/oj), retrieved 2026-09-18 (OJ L 87, 31.3.2017 (original text))
- **Controls:** [ctl-audit-trail](#ctl-audit-trail), [ctl-worm-storage](#ctl-worm-storage)
- **Confidence:** medium; review due 2027-03-18

> (a) the competent authority is able to access them readily and to reconstitute each key stage of the processing of each transaction; (b) it is possible for any corrections or other amendments, and the contents of the records prior to such corrections or amendments, to be easily ascertained; (c) it is not possible for the records otherwise to be manipulated or altered;

<a id="eu-mifid2-art16-6-mifir25"></a>

### Order and transaction data kept five years

`eu-mifid2-art16-6.mifir25` · retention · applies to Investment firms

Keep the relevant data on every order and transaction in financial instruments, whether on own account or for a client, at the competent authority's disposal for five years.

- **Retention:** **5 years**. Trigger: The Article states the period without naming its start.
- **Source:** [Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 (MiFIR), Article 25(1)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2014/600/oj), retrieved 2026-09-18 (OJ L 173, 12.6.2014 (original text))
- **Controls:** [ctl-retention-schedule](#ctl-retention-schedule)
- **Confidence:** medium; review due 2027-03-18

> 1. Investment firms shall keep at the disposal of the competent authority, for five years, the relevant data relating to all orders and all transactions in financial instruments which they have carried out, whether on own account or on behalf of a client.

<a id="eu-mifid2-art16-6-recordings"></a>

### Recorded calls and electronic communications kept five years, up to seven on request

`eu-mifid2-art16-6.recordings` · retention · applies to Investment firms dealing on own account or providing client order services

Keep recordings of relevant telephone conversations and electronic communications for five years, or up to seven years where the competent authority requests it, and provide them to the client on request.

- **Retention:** **5 years**; up to 7 years if the authority requests it. Trigger: The Article states the period without naming its start.
- **Source:** [Directive 2014/65/EU, Article 16(7)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2014/65/oj), retrieved 2026-09-18 (OJ L 173, 12.6.2014 (original text))
- **Controls:** [ctl-communications-capture](#ctl-communications-capture), [ctl-regulator-production](#ctl-regulator-production), [ctl-retention-schedule](#ctl-retention-schedule)
- **Confidence:** medium; review due 2027-03-18

> The records kept in accordance with this paragraph shall be provided to the client involved upon request and shall be kept for a period of five years and, where requested by the competent authority, for a period of up to seven years.

<a id="eu-mifid2-art16-6-records"></a>

### Keep records of all services, activities and transactions sufficient for supervision

`eu-mifid2-art16-6.records` · creation · applies to Investment firms

Keep records of every service, activity and transaction that are sufficient for the competent authority to supervise, enforce, and confirm compliance with obligations to clients and to market integrity. The Article itself sets no retention period.

- **Source:** [Directive 2014/65/EU, Article 16(6)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2014/65/oj), retrieved 2026-09-18 (OJ L 173, 12.6.2014 (original text))
- **Note:** Article 16(6) has no duration. The periods that apply to these records come from Article 16(7) for communications and MiFIR Article 25(1) for orders and transactions.
- **See also:** `eu-mifid2-art16-6.dr72`, `eu-mifid2-art16-6.recordings`, `eu-mifid2-art16-6.mifir25`
- **Controls:** [ctl-records-register](#ctl-records-register)
- **Confidence:** medium; review due 2027-03-18

> 6. An investment firm shall arrange for records to be kept of all services, activities and transactions undertaken by it which shall be sufficient to enable the competent authority to fulfil its supervisory tasks and to perform the enforcement actions under this Directive, Regulation (EU) No 600/2014, Directive 2014/57/EU and Regulation (EU) No 596/2014, and in particular to ascertain that the investment firm has complied with all obligations including those with respect to clients or potential clients and to the integrity of the market.

## Controls

<a id="ctl-audit-trail"></a>

### Tamper-evident audit trail of record creation, modification and deletion

`ctl-audit-trail` · technical · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Log S3 data events for every records bucket to a CloudTrail trail with log file integrity validation. Keep the trail in an Object Lock bucket in a separate log-archive account. Versioning on the records buckets keeps prior content, so a modified record can be re-created. This combination is what the 17a-4(f)(2)(i)(A) audit-trail alternative requires. Firms that choose the WORM option still need an input audit system under 17a-4(f)(3)(iii), and this trail provides it.

- **Satisfies here:** [`eu-mifid2-art16-6.dr72`](#eu-mifid2-art16-6-dr72)
- **Evidence:**
  - CloudTrail trail configuration with data events on the records buckets and LogFileValidationEnabled true
  - Periodic output of validate-logs showing the digest chain intact
  - Log-archive bucket Object Lock configuration
- **AWS:**
  - [AWS CloudTrail (data events, log file integrity validation)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-log-file-validation-intro.html): Organization trail, S3 data events for records buckets, log file validation on, delivered to a locked log-archive bucket
  - [AWS CloudTrail Lake](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.html): Event data store for queryable retention of the same events
- **Limits:** CloudTrail records API actions, not business-level edits made inside an application database. An application that changes records before writing them to S3 needs its own audit trail.

<a id="ctl-communications-capture"></a>

### Capture and retain business communications and recorded calls

`ctl-communications-capture` · technical · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Route every approved business communication channel (email, chat, recorded telephony) to capture that writes into the WORM records buckets under the communications retention class. For telephony on Amazon Connect, send call recordings to a locked bucket. Channels that cannot be captured are prohibited for business use, mirroring the Article 16(7) duty to prevent unrecordable communications on private equipment.

- **Satisfies here:** [`eu-mifid2-art16-6.recordings`](#eu-mifid2-art16-6-recordings)
- **Evidence:**
  - Channel inventory showing the capture path for each approved channel
  - Connect instance storage configuration pointing recordings at the locked bucket
  - Surveillance sampling reports that confirm capture completeness
- **AWS:**
  - [Amazon Connect call recording](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/set-up-recordings.html): Recordings delivered to an Object Lock bucket under the communications retention class
- **Limits:** Capturing third-party messaging apps needs vendor archiving connectors, which are outside this corpus.

<a id="ctl-records-register"></a>

### Register of required records, their producing systems and locations

`ctl-records-register` · organizational · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Maintain a register that maps each record type the rules require to its producing system, owner, retention class and storage location, plus the index keys needed to find any single record. Generate a searchable index (record id, class, dates, account, S3 key) from S3 Inventory and object metadata, queryable with Athena. The same register is the up-to-date system inventory that CFTC 1.31(c)(2)(iii) requires.

- **Satisfies here:** [`eu-mifid2-art16-6.records`](#eu-mifid2-art16-6-records)
- **Evidence:**
  - The register, versioned, reviewed at least as often as this corpus's review cycle
  - Athena query results locating sample records on request, kept as test evidence
  - AWS Config resource inventory for the systems named in the register
- **AWS:**
  - [Amazon Athena over S3 Inventory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/what-is.html): Tables over inventory and metadata exports providing the locate-any-record index
  - [AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/resource-config-reference.html): Resource inventory of the systems in the register

<a id="ctl-regulator-production"></a>

### Tested procedure for producing records to regulators

`ctl-regulator-production` · organizational · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Keep a production runbook covering the request, the locate query against the records register, export in both human-readable and reasonably usable electronic formats with any audit trail, and delivery. Run it on a schedule against sampled records and time each run, so that "promptly" is backed by evidence. The same path serves client requests for MiFID II recordings.

- **Satisfies here:** [`eu-mifid2-art16-6.recordings`](#eu-mifid2-art16-6-recordings)
- **Evidence:**
  - The runbook and the dated results of each production drill, including elapsed time
  - Delivered production packages and their manifests
- **AWS:**
  - [Amazon S3 Batch Operations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/batch-ops.html): Bulk copy of located records and audit-trail extracts into a production bucket

<a id="ctl-retention-schedule"></a>

### Retention schedule mapping record classes to periods and triggers

`ctl-retention-schedule` · organizational · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Keep a retention schedule, generated from this corpus's export, that assigns every record class a period, a trigger and an accessibility window. Put fixed-from-creation classes in buckets whose default retention equals the period. Trigger-based classes (account closure, end of fiscal year, transaction termination, end of the enterprise) cannot know their end date at write time. Write them with the minimum known retention, then extend the retain-until date when the trigger event occurs. Compliance mode allows extending a retention period but never shortening it. Where regimes overlap, take the longest applicable period.

- **Satisfies here:** [`eu-mifid2-art16-6.recordings`](#eu-mifid2-art16-6-recordings), [`eu-mifid2-art16-6.mifir25`](#eu-mifid2-art16-6-mifir25)
- **Evidence:**
  - The retention schedule, versioned, with each row citing an obligation id from this corpus
  - S3 Inventory reports showing each object's retain-until date against the schedule
  - Records of the jobs that extend retention on trigger events, for example S3 Batch Operations manifests and completion reports
- **AWS:**
  - [Amazon S3 Object Lock retention periods](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html): Bucket default retention per record class; per-object retain-until dates extended on trigger events
    <br>*AWS documentation:* “When an object is locked in compliance mode, its retention mode can't be changed, and its retention period can't be shortened.”
  - [Amazon S3 Batch Operations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/batch-ops.html): Bulk retain-until extension when a trigger event (for example account closure) fires
  - [Amazon S3 Inventory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-inventory.html): Daily inventory including Object Lock retain-until date and mode
- **Limits:** The corpus carries the regulatory floor only. Litigation, tax and client-contract retention can exceed it and must be added to the schedule separately.

<a id="ctl-worm-storage"></a>

### Non-rewriteable, non-erasable record storage

`ctl-worm-storage` · technical · confidence medium · review due 2027-03-18

Write regulatory records only to S3 buckets created with Object Lock enabled and a default retention in compliance mode. Compliance mode is the WORM option in Rule 17a-4(f)(2)(i)(B). Governance mode is not, because privileged users can bypass it. Enable versioning (Object Lock requires it) so that a correction is written as a new version and the prior content survives, which is what Delegated Regulation 2017/565 Article 72(1)(b) asks for.

- **Satisfies here:** [`eu-mifid2-art16-6.dr72`](#eu-mifid2-art16-6-dr72)
- **Evidence:**
  - Bucket ObjectLockConfiguration showing ObjectLockEnabled and a DefaultRetention in COMPLIANCE mode
  - AWS Config rule s3-bucket-default-lock-enabled reporting COMPLIANT for every records bucket
  - The Cohasset Associates compliance assessment of S3 Object Lock that AWS links from its documentation, filed with the control evidence
- **AWS:**
  - [Amazon S3 Object Lock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html): Object Lock enabled at bucket creation; default retention mode COMPLIANCE; versioning on
    <br>*AWS documentation:* “S3 Object Lock has been assessed by Cohasset Associates for use in environments that are subject to SEC 17a-4, CFTC, and FINRA regulations.”
  - [AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/s3-bucket-default-lock-enabled.html): Managed rule s3-bucket-default-lock-enabled scoped to the records buckets
- **Limits:** The Cohasset assessment covers the storage layer only. The firm still owns the retention schedule, the audit system for inputs under 17a-4(f)(3)(iii), and the undertakings.
